AUTHOR: C. -Y. Yang; A. Y. S. Tan; M. J. Underwood; C. Bodie; Z. Jiang; S. George; K. Warr; J. -N. Hwang; E. Jones
TITLE: Multi-Object Tracking by Iteratively Associating Detections with Uniform Appearance for Trawl-Based Fishing Bycatch Monitoring
VENUE: 2023 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
SPECIES: 21 species labels (trawl catch/bycatch; species not listed)
DATA: Own NIWA in-trawl camera dataset (5 trips over 13 months); MOT17 half-val
V_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'The uncontrollable environmental conditions, such as low lighting and poor visibility, are presented along with the self-occlusion scenes.'
D2: split by acquisition trip (5 trips); 8 test sequences annotated for MOT
D_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'The training and testing sets are split based on the trips.'
R_EV: Sec. 4.2 / Table 3: 'Tracking on MOT17 Benchmark... our n = 2 version can slightly outperform both OC-SORT and BYTE on the half-val benchmark without tuning'
C_EV: Table 1: 'FP↓ FN↓ IDs↓ ... Ours (n=3) ... 105 199 110' (ID switches measured; threshold values c1, c2 not reported)
E_EV: Sec. 4.1: 'We use the CLEAR metrics [27], including MOTA, IDF1, FP, FN, IDs, and HOTA'; plus top-1/top-3 species accuracy only
ARCH: YOLOX detector + iterative-association tracker built on OC-SORT/BYTE; ResNeXt classifier with track-based voting
METR: MOTA, IDF1, HOTA, FP, FN, IDs, top-1/top-3 accuracy
NOTE: Trip-level split within one campaign (credited under D; not external per P2). R1 = Y only because the tracker is also evaluated on MOT17 (pedestrian benchmark, different detections) with NIWA vs MOT17 MOTA/IDF1 both reported - mechanically R_ALL = Y but this is not a fish-domain external test; verifier should check. C5 credited because ID switches and FPs are measured against GT; confidence threshold values c1/c2 not reported -> C_ALL P. Text is arXiv version of ICIP 2023 paper.
